findings.element: KPI tiles row — sub-labels and prior values
findings.detail: The secondary text beneath each metric tile (prior period values, ranges, footnotes) is rendered at an extremely small size (~7–8px equivalent at dashboard resolution), making it unreadable without zooming in. This is below the minimum body-text threshold for a CEO-grade board deck.

findings.element: 2026 Forecast Scenarios table — 'Key View' column
findings.detail: The narrative text in the 'Key View' column wraps into very small, dense lines that are effectively illegible at normal viewing scale. A board audience cannot read this without zooming.

findings.element: Sector panels (bottom grid) — commentary text blocks
findings.detail: Each sector tile (Passenger Airlines, Hotels, Restaurants, etc.) contains multi-line commentary text that is rendered at ~6–7px equivalent, well below any readable threshold for a board presentation.

findings.element: Key 2025 Actuals & 2026 Macro Themes — bullet body text
findings.detail: The detailed bullet-point paragraphs in the bottom 'Key Themes' section are extremely small and dense, making them illegible at dashboard viewing scale for a CEO/board audience.

findings.element: 2025 Quarterly GDP chart — x-axis label 'Q1 2025'
findings.detail: The leftmost x-axis label appears partially cut off at the left edge of the chart container.

findings.element: 2024 vs 2025 vs 2026F chart — axis labels and bar data labels
findings.detail: The grouped bar chart on the right panel has data labels and x-axis category labels that are extremely small and overlap, making individual values and category names unreadable at board-deck scale.

findings.element: 2024 vs 2025 vs 2026F — Key Macro Indicators bar chart
findings.detail: Data value labels on the grouped bars overlap each other due to the density of bars and small chart area, making individual values indistinguishable.

findings.element: Outlook tab — fc-note commentary block
findings.detail: The commentary block ('Real GDP growth of 2.0% annualized is holding above stall speed…') appears below the KPI tiles and rate tiles but above the charts. However, it is separated from the first chart by a visible gap and tab-navigation row, placing it structurally between UI chrome rather than directly preceding the first chart as required. Depending on scroll position it may not read as 'preceding' the first chart.

findings.element: Outlook tab — fc-note commentary block
findings.detail: The commentary block contains hedging language ('could momentum', 'could prove temporary') and runs to approximately 3 sentences but includes filler qualifiers ('increasingly fragile', 'creates a credible path') that soften rather than assert. Review against forbidden vocabulary list.

findings.element: 2026 Forecast Scenarios table — source footnote row
findings.detail: The sources footnote beneath the forecast table is rendered at a size that is effectively unreadable, which is problematic for a board deck where source attribution must be verifiable.

findings.element: Sector panels grid — bottom two rows vs top row
findings.detail: The vertical spacing between the top row of sector tiles and the second row appears tighter than the spacing between the second and third rows, creating inconsistent gutters across the grid.

findings.element: Sector panel commentary text (all GDP sector cards)
findings.detail: The commentary text beneath each sector mini-chart is rendered at an extremely small font size (appears to be ~6-7px), making it effectively unreadable at normal viewing scale in a board-deck context.

findings.element: Data source / footnote line at very bottom of dashboard
findings.detail: The sources footnote spanning the full width at the bottom of the page is rendered at a font size so small it is illegible, violating minimum body-text size conventions.

findings.element: Annual-chart data vintage / filter bar metadata text
findings.detail: The grey metadata line reading 'ANNUAL-CHART DATA VINTAGE … FILTERED TO ALPHA2 AS-OF 2026-02-01 …' is rendered at a very small size and low contrast against the white background, making it difficult to read.

findings.element: Broad Sector Groups table — source attribution line
findings.detail: The source line beneath the Broad Sector Groups table ('SOURCES: BEA NIP BY INDUSTRY … EY-PARTHENON') is rendered at a near-illegible font size.

findings.element: KPI tile — 'DEBT SERVICE RATIO Q4'20'
findings.detail: The tile header label appears to read 'DEBT SERVICE RATIO Q4'20' but the apostrophe/year suffix is clipped at the tile boundary, and the sub-label text ('% of disp. income / Prior: 12.3% / (Q3 '20)') is visibly cramped and partially cut off on the right edge.

findings.element: KPI tile — 'UNION SENTIMENT MAY'26'
findings.detail: Secondary annotation text inside the Union Sentiment tile appears clipped; the trailing parenthetical reference is cut off at the tile edge.

findings.element: Airlines sector mini-chart (bar chart)
findings.detail: The Airlines sector bar chart shows only a single visible bar with no comparative prior-year bars rendered, making the trend uninterpretable. Peer sector cards all show multiple bars.

findings.element: Cruise Lines sector mini-chart (bar chart)
findings.detail: The Cruise Lines bar chart appears to render only 1-2 bars rather than the full multi-year series shown in peer panels, leaving the chart area largely empty.

findings.element: Sector status badges — 'Trend Concern' vs 'Recession Risk' color coding
findings.detail: Several sector cards use a dark-red/maroon badge labeled 'Recession Risk' while others use an orange badge for 'Trend Concern'. At small scale these colors are difficult to distinguish from each other and from the 'critical' red used in KPI tiles, creating ambiguity about severity hierarchy.

findings.element: GDP Commentary block vs. KPI metric tiles
findings.detail: The GDP Commentary section and the five summary metric tiles (Real GDP 2025, Real Growth 2025, Nominal GDP, 2026F Consensus, GDP Deflator, 2070E Real CAGR) appear to share the same horizontal band with inconsistent vertical alignment — the tiles sit slightly lower than the commentary text block, creating a ragged baseline.

findings.element: GDP Commentary — 2025 Growth & 2026 Outlook
findings.detail: The commentary block contains hedging language ('credible path', 'could provide temporary offsets') and the phrase 'it is weakening' ends abruptly without a forward-looking action statement. Style guide requires commentary to be direct, hedge-free, and 2–4 sentences; this block reads as 2 very long run-on sentences that blur into each other.

findings.element: Sector mini-chart axis labels
findings.detail: Some sector cards (e.g., Software/Cloud, E-Commerce) display year labels on the x-axis of their bar charts while others (e.g., Ambulatory Care, Food Wholesale) omit them entirely, creating an inconsistent presentation across peer panels on the same tab.

findings.detail: No visual defects detected

findings.detail: No visual defects detected

findings.element: TOP SECTOR metric tile
findings.detail: The 'Top Sector' KPI card displays 'Investmen t Banking' with a line break mid-word, truncating/wrapping 'Investment' incorrectly. This is a clear rendering defect visible at board level.

findings.element: Source footnotes below all charts
findings.detail: Source citation text and methodology footnotes beneath the monthly wage growth chart, the annual history chart, and the sector table are rendered at an extremely small font size (appears to be ~6-7px), making them effectively unreadable without zooming in.

findings.element: Chart subtitle/methodology lines on Monthly Wage Growth chart
findings.detail: The subtitle line beneath 'Monthly Wage Growth — Nominal vs Real YoY%' describing the Atlanta Fed tracker methodology is rendered at very small size and low contrast against the background, making it illegible at normal viewing distance.

findings.element: Wage Growth Commentary — Nominal vs Real (fc-note block)
findings.detail: The commentary text block appears to run very close to or beyond its container boundary on the right side, with text potentially clipped. The dense paragraph is difficult to confirm as fully visible at this resolution.

findings.element: Wage Growth Commentary — Nominal vs Real
findings.detail: The commentary block contains what appears to be more than 4 sentences (the visible paragraph runs through multiple clauses and appears to exceed the 4-sentence maximum), violating the style guide limit for fc-note commentary.

findings.element: Avg Hourly Earnings by Sector chart — x-axis labels
findings.detail: The x-axis value labels on the horizontal bar chart ('Avg Hourly Earnings by Sector — 2025 vs 2024') are extremely small and difficult to read at dashboard viewing scale, particularly the numeric tick labels.

findings.element: Monthly Wage Growth chart — data point labels
findings.detail: Several inline data labels on the nominal and real wage growth lines appear to crowd together in the middle portion of the time series (around mid-2023 to early-2024), creating potential overlap between the nominal and real series annotations.

findings.element: Nominal vs Real Wage Growth Annual History chart — axis and source text
findings.detail: The source/methodology footnote beneath the annual history bar chart is rendered at a very small size consistent with the other footnotes, falling below readable threshold for a board-level presentation.

findings.element: Inflation Breadth — Trimmed-Mean & Median CPI vs Headline (bottom chart)
findings.detail: The chart area displays 'AWAITING FIRST PIPELINE RUN' placeholder text with no data plotted. The series lines (Headline CPI MoM, Trimmed-Mean CPI, Median CPI) are defined in the legend but the chart body is essentially blank with only a faint partial line visible at the far right edge. This would be highly embarrassing in a board deck.

findings.element: Inflation Breadth — Trimmed-Mean & Median CPI vs Headline (bottom chart)
findings.detail: The few visible line segments at the right edge of the chart appear disconnected from any broader series, consistent with a pipeline data gap causing the line to stop and restart rather than render a continuous 24-month series.

findings.element: CPI Commentary — Inflation Trajectory & Fed Implications
findings.detail: The commentary block appears to precede the charts on this tab, which is correct in principle, but the summary metric tiles (CPI YoY, Full Year 2025, Monthly Avg, Stickiest Category, Fastest Rising, Peak) are interleaved between the commentary text and the first chart. If those tiles are considered part of the chart section, the commentary does not strictly 'precede the first chart' as required.

findings.element: CPI Commentary — Inflation Trajectory & Fed Implications
findings.detail: The commentary block contains more than 4 sentences (it runs to approximately 5–6 clauses separated by periods), exceeding the maximum sentence count. Style guide requires 2–4 sentences per commentary note.

findings.element: CPI by Category — MoM Change bar chart (right panel, mid-page)
findings.detail: The axis labels, bar labels, and source note text in this chart are extremely small and low-contrast at dashboard resolution, making individual category names and percentage values unreadable without zooming in significantly. This would be illegible when projected in a board meeting.

findings.element: CPI Category Annual Rates table — footnote/source text
findings.detail: The multi-line source/footnote text beneath the CPI Category Annual Rates table is rendered at a very small font size with low contrast, making it effectively illegible at normal viewing distance.

findings.element: Stickiest Category summary tile
findings.detail: The label 'Transportation Svcs' and value '6.1%' appear compressed within the tile, with 'Transportation Svcs' wrapping awkwardly and the supporting detail text appearing cut off at the tile boundary.

findings.element: Annual chart data vintage / footnote strip (below summary tiles)
findings.detail: The small-caps annotation line ('ANNUAL-CHART DATA VINTAGE: PINNED TO ALPHAS 60-91 2024-09-31 · REFRESH CHECKED: QUARTERLY…') uses a noticeably different font weight and style compared to other body/footnote text elsewhere on the tab, suggesting an inconsistent style application.

findings.element: Bottom section — Inflation Breadth chart vertical spacing
findings.detail: The vertical gap between the CPI Category Annual Rates table / CPI by Category 2022 Peak chart row and the Inflation Breadth chart below it appears substantially larger than the spacing between other chart rows on the same tab, creating visible spacing drift.

findings.detail: The x-axis date labels, y-axis tick labels, and the lengthy source note beneath the chart are rendered at an extremely small font size, making them effectively unreadable at dashboard viewing scale. A board-level audience would not be able to verify the data range or source.

findings.element: Home Price Index — Case-Shiller & FHFA source note
findings.detail: The source attribution text below the chart is rendered at a very small size, well below readable threshold for a CEO-level presentation.

findings.element: 30-Year Mortgage Rate vs Fed Funds Rate source note
findings.detail: Source note text is too small to read without zooming in, inconsistent with board-deck legibility standards.

findings.element: Housing Starts — Single-Family vs Multi-Family source note and axis labels
findings.detail: X-axis year labels and source note are rendered at a very small font size, making them illegible at normal viewing distance.

findings.element: Affordability Index & Months Supply chart axis labels and source note
findings.detail: Both the dual-axis labels and the source note beneath the chart are too small to read, undermining data credibility for a board audience.

findings.element: Metro Home Price Performance table — source note at bottom
findings.detail: The multi-line source attribution at the bottom of the table is rendered at a very small font size and is effectively illegible.

findings.element: Global footer / data lineage text at very bottom of page
findings.detail: The dense paragraph of text at the very bottom of the dashboard is rendered at an extremely small size and is completely unreadable, which could be a compliance or attribution concern.

findings.element: 30-Year Mortgage Rate vs Fed Funds Rate — data point labels
findings.detail: Several data point value labels on both the mortgage rate and fed funds rate lines appear to collide or sit very close together, particularly in the 2004–2008 and 2022–2026 regions, reducing readability.

findings.element: Home Price Index — Case-Shiller & FHFA end-point labels
findings.detail: The terminal value labels for the Case-Shiller and FHFA lines at the right edge of the chart appear to be very close together and may overlap, making individual series values hard to distinguish.

findings.element: Housing Commentary — Affordability Crisis & Lock-In Effect
findings.detail: The commentary block contains five sentences, exceeding the maximum of 4 sentences permitted. Additionally, phrases such as 'continues to' and 'remains structurally impaired' border on hedging filler language.

findings.element: Metro Home Price Performance table — Trend column 'Falling' badges
findings.detail: The 'Falling' trend indicator uses a red color for nearly all metros including Detroit, MI which shows positive appreciation (+5.2% / +4.4%). Applying a 'Falling' label with critical-red coloring to a market described as 'Fastest-appreciating major market' appears semantically inconsistent and may misrepresent the data to a board audience.

findings.element: KPI tile row — top header metrics
findings.detail: The KPI tiles in the top row appear to have slightly uneven widths and the sub-text lines within several tiles (e.g., DEBT SERVICE RATIO, UMICH SENTIMENT) are very tightly packed, with footnote text nearly touching the tile border, suggesting inconsistent internal padding across tiles.

findings.element: KPI tiles row — sub-labels and prior/forecast values
findings.detail: The small annotation text beneath each metric tile (prior values, date labels, range notes) is rendered at what appears to be ~7–8px, making it unreadable at normal viewing distance in a board deck context.

findings.element: Oil Supply Shock Tracker chart — x-axis date labels
findings.detail: The x-axis tick labels on the daily close chart (Section 2, left panel) are extremely small and densely packed, rendering them illegible without zooming in.

findings.element: WTI Price History with Recession Shading chart — x-axis and y-axis labels
findings.detail: Axis labels on the long-run WTI history chart (Section 4, left panel) are rendered at a very small size, making year labels and price levels difficult to read in a board presentation.

findings.element: WTI & Brent Monthly Jan 2022–Feb 2026 chart — axis labels and annotations
findings.detail: Month/year tick labels along the x-axis and the inline chart annotations (e.g., 'Recent shock, Mar 2026') are very small and low-contrast against the chart background, making them hard to read at board-deck scale.

findings.element: Oil Supply Shock Tracker — x-axis date labels
findings.detail: The daily date labels on the x-axis of the shock tracker chart appear to run together without sufficient spacing, creating an overlapping or near-overlapping label strip that is unreadable.

findings.element: Section 4 — Recession Signal History commentary block
findings.detail: The commentary block contains hedging language ('causality is debated', 'Worth monitoring if') and runs to what appears to be a single long run-on sentence rather than 2–4 clean declarative sentences, violating the fc-note copy standard.

findings.element: Full Oil Impact Chain panel — node detail text
findings.detail: The descriptive sub-text beneath each transmission node label (e.g., 'Gasoline retail prices within days of a WTI move…') is rendered at approximately 7px and is effectively illegible at board presentation resolution.

findings.element: Sector Margin Impact table — source footnote
